title: A direct bijective proof of the hook-length formula
publication: Discrete Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science1(1997),53–67
read_scope: Definitions and algorithms in sections2,4–5; proofs in sections6.1–6.4. Figures of the local path comparison and stability on PDF10–12 were displayed.

mapping.arrays: A=P transpose, hook function f=−Q transpose
mapping.order: Column order in the source becomes row order in the book.
mapping.candidate_rule: Source nonnegative hook values become nonpositive Q values; source maximum path code becomes book minimum in D<Q<R.
mapping.boundary: Source P-prime Step1 suppresses the left neighbor at the active-column boundary; after transpose this suppresses the upper neighbor at r=i, omitted from the book.
mapping.discarded_coordinate: The source resets the departed hook coordinate to zero. The book never reads the corresponding departed Q coordinate again, so this omission is observationally irrelevant.

independent_completion: P0594 is independently proved by local path inverses, planar tree order and two min-step barrier inequalities, including both state-stability directions and all boundary cases. No hook-formula counting argument is assumed.
